title: Observability hygiene and pruning retro
summary: Notes and concrete proposals from the post-cleanup retro: how we decide what to prune, owner rotation, dashboard lifecycle, query-cost guardrails, tracing sampling anchors, and a short action plan.
body:
Context:
We ran the first cross-team metric/dashboard cleanup sprint in October. This doc captures what we learned, suggested rules of thumb, and an actionable pruning/playbook we can repeat quarterly. It mixes notes from the retro meeting (choppy) and a proposed lightweight process.

Goals (what success looks like):
- Reduce dashboards by ~25% across infra + serving teams (remove duplicates / low-signal panels).
- Reduce monthly query cost from ad-hoc dashboard panels by 30% (measure via billing tags).
- Cut alert noise: 40% fewer non-actionable alerts within 90 days.
- Clear ownership for every metric + dashboard (owner + steward).
- Repeatable quarterly pruning cadence.

High-level observations from the sprint:
- Lots of near-duplicate metrics: e.g., inference.latency_ms vs inference.p90_latency_ms_created_by_teamX. Duplication leads to multiple panels using slightly different aggregations.
- Many low-use dashboards: ~35% of dashboards had <5 visits/month but still ran expensive queries (high cardinality joins).
- Alert fatigue: several alerts triggered repeatedly because they were set on noisy percentiles instead of SLO-backed bucketing.
- Tracing: spans for long-running batch jobs were too verbose; trace retention + sampling not tuned, causing ingestion spikes.
- Ownership gaps: ~120 metrics with no owner in our registry (or owner left the company).

Pruning eligibility rules (first pass):
Eligible for pruning if ALL of the following are true for 90 days window:
1) Query usage < 3 runs/month (dashboard panels + ad-hoc queries combined).
2) Not referenced by any active alert or on-call runbook.
3) Not part of a current SLI/SLO mapping (check SLO registry).
4) Has a documented replacement or flagged as deprecated in the metric registry.
5) Instrumentation source is >12 months old and not actively maintained.

Exception/keep-if:
- Metrics used in experiments or active investigations (tagged with experiment:*)
- Privacy/compliance-related telemetry (keep unless replaced by compliant variant)

Pruning workflow (proposed lightweight):
1) Discovery: run usage job (monthly) -> produce candidate list with cost estimate and referencing dashboards/alerts. (job: telemetry/usage-jobs#metric-usage)
2) Owner contact: auto-email owners + slack ping with 2-week response window. If owner unresponsive, CC team lead.
3) Freeze & archive: mark metric as deprecated in registry; update docs with replacement guidance. Move dashboards using metric to "needs-review" folder.
4) Decommission after 30 days if no objections: stop instrument ingestion & add a one-line note to metric metadata.
5) Final delete after 90 days from decommission (or keep archived raw samples in cold store for compliance).

Owner rotation and stewardship model:
- Every team must nominate 1 metric steward per quarter. Steward responsibilities: validate candidate list, answer owner pings, shepherd dashboard merges/retirements.
- Steward rotation: 3-month cycles, documented in team handbook.
- If a metric owner leaves, steward becomes owner for 60 days to triage.

Dashboard lifecycle (categorize + actions):
- Retire: obsolete dashboards (product retired, metric removed). Delete after 2-week warning.
- Archive: dashboards with low-use but potential future value -> move to archive folder with snapshot.
- Optimize: dashboards with high cost -> replace expensive panels (reduce cardinality, add pre-aggregated materialized views).
- Merge: dashboards with overlapping responsibilities -> create combined view and retire old ones.

Dashboard triage checklist (quick):
- Panel query cost (estimate tokens / bytes scanned) -> if > cost-threshold, mark for optimization.
- Cardinality: ensure group-by tags limited to supported cardinality (<= 1k unique) or use bucketing.
- Visit frequency: <5 visits/month -> archive candidate.
- Owner assigned? if no -> steward assigns and pings.

Query-cost guardrails (practical steps):
- Add a "query-cost" panel to infra/dashboard-home showing rolling weekly cost per dashboard team tag.
- Encourage use of pre-aggregated tables for token-level metrics (e.g., prefix caches, kv-cache hits aggregated hourly).
- Require EXPLAIN plan for any dashboard panel flagged > $X/month during optimisation run.
- Set query-time limit: 120s on interactive panels; longer queries must be scheduled as batch exports.

Tracing sampling and long-running spans (rules of thumb):
- Sampling tiers:
  * 100%: customer-facing request traces that hit user-facing latencies > SLO threshold in the last 24h (sampling via dynamic trigger).
  * 5%: baseline sampling for production traffic for general health metrics.
  * 0.5%: high-cardinality internal operations unless debug flag enabled.
- Trace anchors: for multi-hop inference (e.g., serve -> model runtime -> kv-cache), ensure a persistent trace-id across hops and capture lightweight span tags (no full payloads).
- Long-run batch jobs: sample based on failure/error signals, not duration. Keep long running spans aggregated (summary spans) rather than full child-span flood.
- PII note: redact user prompt content from spans; store hash if necessary for correlation.

Alert tuning checklist (practical):
- Map every alert to either: SLO/SLI, operational readiness, or security. If not mapped, mark for review.
- Use severity levels (sev1, sev2, sev3) and attach runbooks for sev1/2.
- Add suppression windows for noisy maintenance windows and deploy-burst suppression.
- Prefer ratio-based alerts (error_rate > threshold) over absolute counts when load varies.

Cost measurement + tracking:
- Tag dashboard queries and saved searches with billing_tag:team to attribute costs.
- Add a monthly "observability cost" report to the infra finance sync with top 10 cost drivers.

Action items (owner -> task -> target):
- Ravi Singh: run the metric-usage job end-to-end and validate candidate list by 2024-11-15.
- Maya Thompson: produce dashboard cost report and identify top 20 expensive panels by 2024-11-22.
- Jordan Lee: prototype a pre-agg table for inference.token_counts and replace 3 heavy panels by 2024-12-06.
- Claire Zhao: write a short-owner-email template + set up automated ping workflow in the registry by 2024-11-12.
- Observability team: schedule quarterly pruning window (first week after product sprint) and publish calendar invite (target: Q1 2025).

Quick sample queries (notes to devs):
- Metric usage: SELECT metric_name, count(*) as queries FROM observability.query_log WHERE timestamp > now() - interval '90 days' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY queries ASC;
- Dashboard visits: SELECT dashboard_id, visits FROM dashboard_analytics WHERE range = '90d' ORDER BY visits;
- Cost estimate: use the billing_tag aggregation: SELECT billing_tag, sum(cost_usd) FROM query_billing WHERE ts > now() - interval '30 days' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC;

Open questions / discussion items:
- Retention sweet spot: should we keep raw traces 30 days and aggregates 13 months? finance and compliance need to weigh in.
- Automation vs manual review: how much can we safely auto-deprecate when owner unresponsive? propose: auto-deprecate after 60 days only for metrics with cost < $10/month.
- Should we require a "dashboard steward" for every team with >10 dashboards? (proposal: yes)

Notes to self / meeting snippets (informal):
- Teams appreciated example PRs for 'how to change a metric name'—we should add a cookiecutter PR template.
- Several infra folks asked for better alerts -> map to SLOs first before tuning thresholds.
- Need a small script to snapshot dashboards before archive so owners can restore easily.

References / useful links:
- Confluence: Observability Registry (CONFLUENCE-OBS-842)
- GitHub: telemetry repo PR for usage job: https://github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry/pull/902
- Jira: OPS ticket tracker JIRA-OPS-4567

End of notes. This is intentionally a working draft — will convert into a lightweight playbook once we validate the flow in the next cleanup window.
